# Correction and Status Notice for Four HORIZON SHIELD Working Papers

**Issued:** 2026-07-26 (JST) by Toshikatsu Oga (大賀俊勝), The HORIZONs Inc., ORCID 0009-0000-9180-903X.
**Anchor target:** the SHA-256 of this document is appended to the JIDEC public ledger and timestamped
to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps.

This notice corrects statements in previously published working papers and records changes of fact
that occurred after their publication. It is issued because the papers describe a verification system,
and a verification system whose own published claims drift from what can be measured is worse than
no system at all.

**Nothing in this notice was found by an external reviewer.** Every item below was found by measuring
our own published artifacts against our own published claims on 2026-07-26. We publish it for the
same reason the system exists: a claim that affects what a household pays should be checkable, and
this notice is not exempt.

---

## Papers in scope

| Ref | Title (short) | Version / date used |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | JCCDB v1.2 — Cryptographic Audit Hash and Macroeconomic Price Correction | 2026-05-09 (SSRN 6738701) |
| P2 | Reducing Information Asymmetry in Credence-Good Markets: A Third-Party Verified Quote (VRQ) Framework | v2.4, 2026-05-25 (SSRN 6807738) |
| P3 | Benchmarking Frontier Large Language Models on Consumer-Facing Cost Questions | June 2026 (SSRN 6872819) |
| P4 | Verification for the Buyer, Not the Seller: A Deployed Construction-Quote Gate | 2026-06-19 (SSRN 6964439) |

---

## C1. P1 §3.7 — the dual-path implementation is not an additional reproducibility guarantee

**Published text.** "This dual-path implementation provides an additional reproducibility guarantee:
the hash that the homeowner sees during the chat and the hash printed on their PDF report are
necessarily identical, because either the PDF reuses the chat-computed hash (the principal path) or,
when invoked independently, regenerates an identical hash from the same canonical inputs (the fallback path)."

**Correction.** On the principal path the PDF generator does not recompute the hash; it assigns the
value received from the caller. The two values are therefore identical by construction. An identity
that holds necessarily is not evidence of anything, and the dual path removes rather than adds a
cross-check: on the principal path no second, independent computation of the hash occurs.

The independent evidence for reproducibility in P1 is §6.4, where a Python `hashlib` reference
implementation reproduces the production output byte-for-byte. That result stands. It establishes
the determinism of the hash **function**; it does not establish that the production **path** computes
the hash twice, and P1 should not be read as claiming that it does.

**Status of the mechanism itself:** unchanged and correctly documented. P1 §3.7 prints the actual
code, including the branch that assigns the caller-supplied value. The defect is in the inference
drawn from the mechanism, not in its disclosure.

## C2. P1 §5.3 — strong consistency does not establish immutability

**Published text.** "R2's strong consistency directly supports the reproducibility property of
Section 3: any two diagnostics with identical inputs read the identical dataset version, compute
identical `adjAvg` values, and therefore produce identical audit hashes."

**Correction.** Strong consistency guarantees that all clients observe the same current object state.
It does not guarantee that the object state does not change. If the reference dataset is replaced,
two diagnostics performed before and after the replacement read different content.

This interacts with a second property documented in the same paper. The date component of the audit
hash input is constructed at month resolution (P1 §5.2). A replacement of the reference dataset within
a single calendar month therefore leaves the hash input string unchanged while the underlying data
differs, and the change is not detectable from the hash.

**Consequence.** The audit hash commits to the declared input fields, not to the version or content
of the reference dataset. This is a scope limitation of the mechanism and should have been stated in
P1 §6.6. It is stated here.

## C3. P1 — declared scope of the audit hash

For the avoidance of doubt, the audit hash input comprises region, work category, quoted amount,
computed adjusted average, and date at month resolution. It does **not** commit to: the version or
content of the reference dataset; the deployed War Price Coefficient value; the commit identifier of
the diagnostic algorithm; threshold values; or the generated PDF document itself.

This is a design boundary rather than a defect, but it was not stated as a limitation and could
therefore be read more broadly than intended.

## C4. P2 §4 — "institutionally independent body" is withdrawn

**Published text.** "The certifying function is assigned to JIDEC, an institutionally independent body
planned for operation from June 2026, whose role is record-keeping neutrality rather than commercial gain."

**Correction.** JIDEC is operated by The HORIZONs Inc., the same company that operates the commercial
assessment service. It is not institutionally independent, and the phrase is withdrawn.

What can be claimed instead, and is now measurable, is narrower and different in kind: JIDEC is a
public, append-only ledger designed so that no trust in its operator is required. Every published
result can be re-derived from bytes a reader fetches and hashes independently. Operator independence
is not established by this design and is not claimed.

P2 v2.4's own revision note already acknowledged that "the institutional design that would guarantee
JIDEC's independence ... is acknowledged as unresolved and is left to future work." This notice makes
that acknowledgment explicit in the body rather than in the appendix.

---

## U1. P2 §4 — JIDEC is operational as of 2026-07-26

P2 v2.4 states that JIDEC is "planned for operation from June 2026" and its revision note states that
it "is not yet operational as of this writing." As of 2026-07-26 it is operational. Measured state at
time of issue: six ledger entries, all confirmed in the Bitcoin blockchain (blocks 959118, 959492,
959492, 959534, 959634, 959634); a machine-readable catalog at `/.well-known/api-catalog` (RFC 9727);
an agent card (A2A v1.0.1); a security contact (RFC 9116); citation resolution at `/cite/{citation}`;
a machine-readable verification recipe at `/verify/{n}`; server-side replay of anchored verification
paths; and a read-only MCP endpoint conforming to protocol revision 2025-11-25.

The service publishes its own limits at `/health` under `transparency`, including that it is **not**
a conformant SCITT Transparency Service and that OpenTimestamps holds no RFC, ISO, ETSI or eIDAS
standing. Auditors requiring an institutionally recognised timestamp should additionally require an
RFC 3161 or eIDAS qualified timestamp.

## U2. P1 §5.5 — worker source code is no longer closed

P1 states "Worker source code remains closed." As of 2026-07-26 the deployed source of the ledger
service and of its MCP interface is published in the public repository, and the full source of the
PDF generation worker is anchored byte-for-byte as JIDEC ledger entry #4 (Bitcoin block 959534).

## U3. P3 §5 — the governance arrangement now exists

P3 notes that "the authors are exploring a transparent, externally verifiable arrangement" for the
question of who controls and verifies a structured reference. That arrangement is the JIDEC ledger
described in U1. P3's empirical results are unaffected; no figure, table or measurement in P3 changes.

---

## Corrections to published dataset statistics

The twenty anchored diagnosis receipts published at
`https://shield.the-horizons-innovation.com/souba/kajou-seikyu-jirei-20/` were recomputed from their
canonical bytes on 2026-07-26. The dataset summary previously published in the English-language pages
and in the dataset repository did not match those bytes.

| Quantity | Correct (recomputed from anchored bytes) | Previously published |
|---|---|---|
| Mean overcharge | ¥1,009,500 | ¥830,000 (pages, README) / ¥825,000 (dataset header) |
| Minimum overcharge | ¥350,000 | ¥120,000 |
| Maximum overcharge | ¥2,800,000 | ¥2,820,000 |
| Prefectures covered | 16 | 15 |
| Case count, maximum rate | 20, 84.9% | unchanged, correct |

The mean and the minimum were previously understated; the maximum was overstated by ¥20,000.
A separately published return-on-fee figure of "145x" could not be derived from the quantities stated
alongside it and has been withdrawn; the quotient of the corrected mean over the stated fee is 18.4.

**Sampling.** These twenty cases are not a random sample of renovation transactions. They are
diagnoses in which overcharging was found. The mean above describes the size of an overcharge when
one is found. It is not an expected return for an arbitrary estimate.

## Correction to a published anchor proof

The OpenTimestamps proof published alongside the PTKA methodology declaration contained only pending
calendar attestations until 2026-07-26 and therefore did not, on its own, establish the Bitcoin block
height stated beside it. The proof has since been upgraded and now contains Bitcoin block header
attestations for blocks 949320 and 949356. The declaration's SHA-256 is unchanged and matches the
value published previously:
`596da30ba4ca731f21efaa1c4a6537290e996e0f039cbe57704de1674e4a0282`.

The stated block height was correct. It was not verifiable from the published proof file until the
date of this notice, and readers who attempted to verify it before that date could not have done so.

---

## Naming conflict to be aware of

P1 defines the audit hash as a SHA-256 digest truncated to twelve hexadecimal characters. The field
named `audit_hash` in the published diagnosis receipts is a twelve-character case identifier that is
not hexadecimal and is not that digest. The receipts are verifiable by a different and independent
route — the SHA-256 of each receipt's canonical bytes together with its OpenTimestamps proof — and
that route is unaffected. A reader cross-checking the receipts against P1 should not expect the
`audit_hash` field to reproduce under P1 §3.

---

## What this notice does not claim

It does not claim that any empirical result in P1 §6, P2 §5, P3 §3 or P4 §6 is affected. No figure,
table, or measurement in those sections is changed by this notice.

It does not claim that the corrections above are exhaustive. They are what was found by one pass over
our own artifacts on one day. If a reader finds a published figure that cannot be reproduced from the
anchored bytes, that figure is wrong and we would like to be told.

It does not claim institutional independence for JIDEC, and does not claim that JIDEC's design
resolves the conflict of interest inherent in operating a commercial assessment service.

---

## How to verify this notice

This document's SHA-256 is appended to the JIDEC ledger and timestamped to Bitcoin. To check it
without trusting the issuer: fetch the canonical bytes of the ledger entry, compute their SHA-256
yourself, confirm it equals the cited entry identifier, and confirm the OpenTimestamps proof against
the Bitcoin blockchain. The procedure is published at
`https://hs-ledger.oga-surf-project.workers.dev/llms.txt` and the machine-readable form at
`/verify/{n}`.

The dataset corrections can be checked independently of the ledger: fetch `claim.txt` from each of
the twenty receipts, sum `reduction_amount_jpy`, and divide by twenty.

## 日本語要約

本通知は、公開済みの作業論文4本の記述を訂正し、公開後に変わった事実を記録するものである。
**外部から指摘されたものは1件も無い。**すべて 2026-07-26 に、自社の公開物を自社の公開主張と
突き合わせて測った結果である。

訂正は4点。P1 §3.7 の dual-path は「追加の再現性保証」ではない（主経路では再計算ではなく代入である）。
P1 §5.3 の「R2 の強整合性が再現性を支える」は成り立たない（強整合性は不変性ではなく、date が月解像度の
ため同一月内の差し替えを検知できない）。P1 の監査ハッシュが何をコミットしていないかを明記した。
そして P2 §4 の「institutionally independent body」を**撤回する**——JIDEC を運営しているのは同じ会社である。

更新は3点。JIDEC は 2026-07-26 に稼働した。P1 の「Worker source code remains closed」はもう正しくない。
P3 が「探索中」と書いた統治上の取り決めは実在するようになった。

さらに、公開していた20件のデータセット統計が、錨を打ったバイト列と一致していなかった。
平均は ¥830,000 ではなく **¥1,009,500**、最小は ¥120,000 ではなく **¥350,000**、
最大は ¥2,820,000 ではなく **¥2,800,000**、都道府県数は15ではなく**16**である。
**平均と最小は過小に、最大だけ過大に公表していた。**導出できなかった「145倍」は撤回した。
そして20件は無作為抽出ではなく、過剰請求が見つかった事例である。

PTKA 宣言の OpenTimestamps 証明は、2026-07-26 まで pending のみで、併記していたブロック高を
それ自体では立証していなかった。現在は #949320 と #949356 の確定証明を含む。宣言文のハッシュは
公表値と一致しており変わっていない。**ブロック高の主張は正しかったが、この日まで読者には検証できなかった。**

**本通知は網羅的であるとは主張しない。**1日の1回の走査で見つかったものである。
錨を打ったバイト列から再現できない数字を見つけた読者は、その数字が誤りなので、知らせてほしい。
